title: Beyond Quotas: The Dynamics of Preferential EV Import Arrangements in Armenia
content:
Preferential import arrangements can influence electric vehicle (EV) market development, consumer access, and the transition toward lower-emission transport. This study examines the evolution of Armenia’s preferential EV import arrangements during 2020–2026, focusing on regulatory changes, quota allocation, reported utilization, and policy implications. It employs descriptive and comparative analysis based on publicly available legal acts, official government announcements, and administrative data.
The findings distinguish the general customs-duty exemption applied in 2020–2021 from the subsequent quota-based arrangements. In 2022, Armenia’s EAEU-level allocation was 7,000 vehicles, while the national implementation limit was 6,400. The EAEU-level allocation reached 8,000 vehicles annually during 2023–2025, although differences in national implementation rules and data availability constrain the calculation of comparable annual utilization rates. In 2024, the national quota was increased from 7,400 to 8,000 vehicles and was fully utilized, according to official administrative information. In 2026, the initial allocation of 15,000 vehicles was increased by an additional 5,000, bringing the total quota to 20,000. Reported administrative figures indicate that 18,221 quota places had been utilized by 3 October 2026, corresponding to an interim utilization rate of approximately 91.1%.
The findings underscore the importance of transparent allocation rules, consistent ad-ministrative reporting, and systematic monitoring of quota utilization. They also demonstrate that regulatory differences and gaps in annual data limit direct comparisons across the study period. The study provides a descriptive evidence base for improving the transparency, monitoring, and effectiveness of Armenia’s preferential EV import policy.
